mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate indicates tight monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by 5% YoY but the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 5% but the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 35% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic activity, which should lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is positive but the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) outpaces inflation (CPIAUCSL), real economic growth is positive, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate exceeds CPIAUCSL growth rate
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth exceeds CPIAUCSL growth but the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth is positive but the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 35% of periods, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which supports economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by 1% YoY but the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and unemployment (UNRATE) is low, it indicates tightening monetary conditions, which should lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5% and UNRATE is below 5%
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5% and UNRATE is below 5% but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 35% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.
